models.label: MusicGen Stereo Melody Large
models.priceBasis: The rate this model shipped with, unchanged. Two things it does not capture: Replicate bills prediction RUNTIME (GPU-seconds) while this sells generated seconds, which are not proportional and have a fixed boot cost that makes the shortest clips the thinnest margin; and input_audio lengthens the prediction while the price is computed from duration_seconds alone, so a long reference track is provider time nobody is billed for. Re-derive from Replicate's hardware rate before selling on a platform key.

models.label: MusicGen Melody Large (mono)
models.priceBasis: Same rate as musicgen-stereo-melody-large, which is the safe direction: mono melody is the SAME Replicate model family doing less work than the stereo variant it is priced from. Replicate bills prediction RUNTIME (GPU-seconds), not generated audio seconds, and the two are not proportional: there is a fixed boot cost, so the shortest clips are the thinnest margin on every per-second model on this API. Re-derive from Replicate's hardware rate and a timed prediction before selling on a platform key. Note also that input_audio lengthens the prediction while the price is computed from duration_seconds alone, so a long reference track is provider time nobody is billed for.

models.label: ElevenLabs Flash v2.5
models.priceBasis: 0.1 credits per character. ElevenLabs bills the whole Flash and Turbo family at 0.5 of ITS credits per character, which at Creator rates is about $0.00011/char. A credit COSTS $0.001 and SELLS for $0.0007 at the subscription floor, so 0.1 credits returns about $0.00007 against $0.00011 of provider cost: this is sold at a LOSS at the floor and near break-even on pay-as-you-go, well short of the 1.4x the rest of this catalogue clears. Kept as the shipped rate because changing a published price is the platform owner's decision, and the three models that quote this one are priced alike so that choosing between them is never a choice about margin. It is one decision for the whole Flash and Turbo family, and eleven-multilingual-v2 at 0.2 credits against 1 EL credit per character carries exactly the same exposure.

models.label: Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (Nano Banana)
models.priceBasis: Google's published price for one Gemini 2.5 Flash image is $0.039, doubled to 78 credits. Aspect ratio does not move it: Google bills the image, and every ratio it accepts is the same image. imageConfig.imageSize WOULD move it, and this descriptor deliberately does not map it. What a caller CAN still move is the input: input_image takes up to three source images and Google bills their tokens by area, so a call with three large sources costs more than this flat price was computed for. It is a FLOOR on any editing use.

models.label: Gemini 3 Pro Image

Aspect ratio does not move the price; imageConfig.imageSize would, and is not mapped. The input does move it: up to three source images, billed by area, against a flat price. It is a FLOOR on any editing use.

models.label: OpenAI GPT Image 2 edit (low)
models.priceBasis: The rate this tier carried before edits were split by orientation, kept unchanged. An edit is NOT priced like a generation: OpenAI bills the returned image PLUS the caller's input image, whose token count scales with its area, so this flat price is a FLOOR. The exposure is largest on the low tiers, where the input can cost more than the output: a 1024x1024 source is between ~320 and ~1024 image-input tokens depending on the model's tiling, i.e. $0.003 to $0.010 at $10 per million, against a $0.006 low-quality output. Settle it with one POST to the edits endpoint and read usage.input_tokens_details back. Raise it in Settings > Platform Keys before selling edits of big images on a platform key. Only the square tiers are sold here for that reason: an orientation tier would multiply the same uncapped input cost across three times as many ids, and an edit normally keeps the shape of the image it was given.

models.label: Seedance 2.5 (720p)
models.priceBasis: The per-second rate above predates this note and carries no recorded basis; what follows explains the MODIFIERS only. Per-file modifiers are a PLATFORM surcharge and not a ByteDance rate: ModelArk bills Seedance per token, an image handed to it as an opening frame, a closing frame or a reference conditions every step of the generation, and the platform additionally reads the file out of storage and inlines it into the request as a data URL, which the per-second rate above was not computed for. 0.05 per file is a FLOOR chosen because ByteDance publishes no per-image figure. The most a call on this model can reach is 1.2x, from its four reference images; this model has no frame slots. It can only over-charge against a rate nobody has published. A MODIFIER is not editable in Settings > Platform Keys, which publishes the rate and the clamps: it lives in this descriptor, so changing it is an edit here plus a re-import. Lower it that way once the token cost of an input image is known.

models.label: Grok Imagine Video
